text:
alexa: I want to float a small, composable rollout metadata shape that leans on pointers rather than embedding orchestration. goal: make pin/rollout intent easy to read for ops and compatible with Dedicated/Private.

I propose fields: rollout_policy (cohorts list), lease (heartbeat + ttl), alert_refs (list of alert ids), snapshot_on_pin (boolean), fallback_model (single string), and soft_unpin (bool with backoff).

tom: can you show a tiny example of what that looks like?

alexa: quick pseudo example below, still terse:```json
{
  "rollout_policy": [{"name":"canary","pct":3},{"name":"region-eu","pct":40}],
  "lease": {"ttl_secs":"3600","heartbeat_required":"true"},
  "alert_refs": ["ap-33","ap-99"],
  "snapshot_on_pin": "true",
  "fallback_model": "redwood/gptx-5b@v2",
  "soft_unpin": "true",
  "reconcile_window_secs": "900"
}
```

nina: I like lease + heartbeat idea. helps with orphaned pins when control-plane loses connectivity. is snapshot_on_pin intended to capture example inputs/outputs? will that be PII-safe?

alexa: snapshot_on_pin is intended to capture minimal evaluation metrics and a small input sample for postmortem — we should gate it behind a tenant flag and KMS. metadata only stores a pointer to the snapshot record. not the raw payload.

chris: alert_refs as a list is nice because teams often want multiple signals (latency + semantic-quality + infra-error-rate). but prefer alert_refs be authoritative only for soft_unpin decisions. full auto-unpin should require an explicit "allow_auto_unpin" flag per rollout.

alexa: good point. change to: alert_refs + allow_auto_unpin = false by default. soft_unpin means: reduce cohort pct to zero over a backoff instead of immediate unpin. less noisy.

ops-bot: NOTICE: rollout request accepted: model redwood/gptx-11b@v4 by alexa at 3532109876. policy: canary(3%), region-eu(40%).

nina: we need to be clear about precedence: customer_pin > snapshot_on_pin (customer snapshot) > rollout_policy > resolver. document this in RFC. also TTL semantics: if lease expires without heartbeat the runtime should treat the rollout_policy as suspended, not deleted.

chris: operationally, add an audit pointer: on any soft_unpin/unpin, we emit an audit event with fields: rollout_id, model_id, trigger_alerts, timestamp, chosen_fallback. put that in the audit store not the primary metadata.

tom: SDK compatibility note: avoid nested objects with runtime-only types in top-level schema. for Dedicated/Private, store compact strings for lease & flags (we can parse into richer types in server). reduces SDK churn.

alexa: agreed. keep top-level compact and stable. the control-plane only needs to store pointers and small flags. runtime pulls alert definitions and executes unpin flows.

nina: one more thing: add reconcile_window to define how long after a pin change the system waits before asserting convergence across dedicated clusters. helps reduce flapping during big rebalances. default 15m.

chris: i'll draft the audit-event spec and minimal runtime playbook for soft_unpin vs hard_unpin. include sample CLI commands for manual rollback and an emergency kill switch.

tom: i'll test SDK roundtrip for the compact fields and ensure serialization works for Private air-gapped deployments.

alexa: great. i'll update the RFC with the compact schema, precedence table, and example CLI snippets. tagging you all when PR is up. :rocket:
